question: A 21-year-old man went to the emergency room after presenting several episodes of generalized tonic-clonic seizures in the last week. In the cranial CT scan, a unilocular cystic lesion was observed with a small nodule attached to the wall corresponding to the encysting larva of a parasite. Which of the following pathogens can be responsible ?:
analysis: The presence of a unilocular cystic lesion with an encysting larva in the cranial CT scan suggests a parasitic infection. Among the options provided, Taenia solium is the pathogen responsible for causing neurocysticercosis, which is characterized by the development of cystic lesions in the brain due to the larval stage of the pork tapeworm Taenia solium.
